title: Postmarked
style: cinematic horror film still, dramatic moody lighting with the subject clearly visible and centered, quiet old American town in late winter, rain-slick brick streets and gaslight-style lamps, vintage cream envelopes with red wax seals and dried roses, faded rose and slate blue tones, adults only, film grain, 35mm, highly detailed, subject clearly visible, no text, no watermark
caption:
Part 1. A love letter mailed in 1975 just arrived. 💌

Original fiction. Part 2 tomorrow night.

#scarystories #horrorstory #creepy #storytime #fyp

scenes.narration: The letter in Ben Hartley's mailbag was mailed in 1975. And the envelope was still warm.
scenes.image: a cream envelope with a red wax seal resting on top of a stack of mail in a canvas mailbag

scenes.narration: Ben has walked the same mail route in Fernhill for nineteen years. Every dog. Every porch step. Every crack in the sidewalk.
scenes.image: a middle-aged mail carrier in a rain jacket walking a wet brick street at dawn

scenes.narration: One grey February morning, he found it in his bundle. Cream paper. Red wax seal. A faint smell of roses. Addressed by hand to Thomas, 42 Wren Street.
scenes.image: a cream envelope with a red wax seal on a post office sorting table, blurred handwriting, a dried rose petal beside it

scenes.narration: The postmark said February, 1975. The stamp cost eight cents.
scenes.image: close-up of an old faded postage stamp with a rose design and wavy cancellation lines

scenes.narration: No barcode. No forwarding label. It hadn't come in on any truck. It was just there, on top, like someone had placed it.
scenes.image: a mail carrier frowning at an envelope under the fluorescent lights of an empty sorting room

scenes.narration: Old mail turns up, his supervisor said. Stuck behind a machine for fifty years. But the paper wasn't yellow. The ink wasn't faded. It looked like it was written last night.
scenes.image: a pristine cream envelope held up to a window, rain streaking the glass behind it

scenes.narration: Ben shouldn't have read it. He knows that. But the wax had already cracked.
scenes.image: a man's hands holding an envelope with a cracked red wax seal

scenes.narration: My dearest Thomas. Every day without you is February. Love, Evelyn.
scenes.image: a handwritten love letter on cream paper, script blurred and unreadable, a pressed red rose on top

scenes.narration: That afternoon he walked it to Wren Street himself.
scenes.image: a mail carrier walking down a quiet tree-lined street of old houses in cold drizzle

scenes.narration: Number 42 was boarded up. The yard was a tangle of dead brambles. But the mailbox at the gate was brand new. And its little red flag was up.
scenes.image: a shiny new mailbox with its red flag raised in front of a boarded-up Victorian house
